summary: The candidate is a partial fix. It adds the missing local DiffGenerator sleep, wake, and disk-refit methods and correctly normalizes the previously reported scheduler ConnectionError/TimeoutError cases. It does not qualify the complete original diffusion feature contract: no real diffusion checkpoint completed sleep, wake, generation, and refit; no kill/relaunch comparison was run; and FSDP sleep/wake remains unsupported. Malformed scheduler response objects can also leak raw AttributeError.

tests.what_was_measured: ConnectionError and TimeoutError are normalized and chained; declared error, non-dict, negative, and success payloads are handled; None/missing-output response objects leak AttributeError.
One synthetic torch.nn.Linear sleep/wake numerical controller round trip passed on AMD Instinct MI355X; it does not cover the candidate transport surface end to end.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI355X / ROCm 7.2 synthetic controller round trip passed. This exercises controller code already in base, not a real diffusion checkpoint or end-to-end DiffGenerator transport.

native_rebuild_reason: No native C/C++/HIP/Rust source changed between the recorded base and candidate, so rebuilding native code was not applicable.
remaining_counterexamples: No real diffusion checkpoint was run through sleep, wake, generation, and disk refit, so model-specific correctness and memory behavior remain unverified.
No end-to-end sleep+wake+refit versus kill-and-relaunch timing comparison was supplied, despite being an explicit original-issue objective.
FSDP inference sleep/wake remains explicitly unsupported and raises RuntimeError.
The GPU round trip exercises MemoryOccupationController code present in the base, not the candidate's new DiffGenerator transport surface end to end.
A scheduler response of None or an object missing output leaks AttributeError rather than a lifecycle-specific RuntimeError.
remaining_limitations: Only one AMD Instinct MI355X was available; CUDA-specific behavior was not tested.
No diffusion model weights/checkpoint were available. The tiny Llama fixture is transport-only and cannot qualify diffusion behavior, so it was not used.
Distributed and FSDP behavior, real generation/refit numerical correctness, memory savings, and comparative relaunch timing remain unverified.
No native rebuild was performed because the candidate changes no native source.
